ARC Raiders suffers from not knowing if it wants to be a true PvP or PvE game which is a frustrating experience to play as some one who has maybe 5-10 hours a week to game. 

On one hand I get it its an extraction shooter so if you drop your guard don't be surprised if you get killed by a random raider in your area. But this game promotes the laziest possible method of PvP'ers by basically encouraging extract camping. You get a bunch of loot that'll help you increase your hideout production? Well head to an extract that has a brainrotted raider who sat there 20 minutes scrolling through tiktok who became aware you wanted to leave by making the extract have a loud notification. While I only died to it once its still annoying knowing that all people have to do is sit in a bush to have a successful raid. It's even more annoying when you get shot first and then shoot back but the game still takes into account that you were involved in a PvP moment and decides your matchmaking is going to be focused on more PvP lobbies. ♥♥♥♥ off with that. 

I can forgive all this because I know what kind of game it is, but ARC Raiders genuinely feels like it was built as PvE extraction shooter first and then a last second decision was made to enable PvP. All the starting weapons feel like they were designed to fight ARCs and not Raiders. All the loot feels like it ARC focused and not player focused. I genuinely don't see the point PvP when the game doesn't include any kind of incentive to engage with another player. There's no special loot, there's no exclusive items, and there's no incentive to engage in PvP other than screw over another player. In Tarkov for example there's specific quest lines that require in PvP that allow you to get certain in game items in shops through rewards or leveling up the trader. In ARC Raiders, from what I researched, there's no quest line and no in game incentives to fight another player. So what's the point of including in the game? I play competitive games and I play games that pits you against other players, but the way this game was made its feels like it didn't want to be any of that. I'm not against PvP in games, but what I'm against is pointless PvP where there's no in-game incentive. 

I know there's PvE update coming to this game, but after the short amount of time I had with this game and the experience with the community its a hard no for me. From what I understand that update is only a trial period to get data and player feedback. So its not going to be a permanent mode from what I understand. If it ever decides to make it an actual mode you can chose or have an actual incentive to PvP I'd probably revisit ARC Raiders again. 

I wish I could give this a "Mixed" review because Embark did make it free for people like me to try. I do think that developers that allow people to play their online games like this are genuinely good for consumers. Even though it wasn't for me it might be for you. If you can enjoy a game that has PvP for the sake of PvP then there's allot for you here. If you need bit of an incentive to have that PvP then it isn't here.

I think this game is absolutely brilliant, and I still haven’t found another game with a similar style that offers quite the same experience. What makes it so interesting is how looting and combat are equally important, and how you can never really know whether another raider you encounter is actually friendly.

The game’s community is basically split into two main groups. On one side, there are the PvP players, who tend to be hostile and some particularly mean ones are referred to as „rats” by the community. On the other side, there are the PvE players, who are generally friendly, sometimes even sharing loot with each other and teaming up to fight ARCs.

Fortunately, the game tracks your behavior and uses it to match you with players who are likely to have a similar playstyle. I’ve tried both PvE and PvP lobbies, and while both are fun, I personally think PvE lobbies are much more efficient for looting in the long run.

There’s a huge variety of weapons available, both for fighting ARCs and for PvP. The developers regularly add new weapons to the game, giving players even more options to experiment with. Each weapon feels unique and caters to a different playstyle.

The optimization is also pretty decent. Even on lower-end PCs, the game can still be enjoyable with reduced graphics settings, especially considering how poorly optimized many other Unreal Engine 5 games are. And if you have a powerful PC, the game looks absolutely gorgeous even on settings just above medium.

A lot of people complain about cheaters, but personally, I haven’t encountered that many. Of course, there have been a few occasions when the developers refunded my lost gear because of cheaters. The important thing is that the developers seem to be putting a lot of effort into combating cheating.

Another really interesting detail is how the physical movement of the ARCs was developed. Instead of manually programming all their movements, they used self-learning AI, essentially telling it to learn how to walk and fight using a specific set of legs and equipment.

The game also has several ways of keeping players engaged for hundreds of hours. You can spend an incredible amount of time crafting and upgrading weapons. Collecting blueprints is another huge motivation, especially for newer players. And since the Frozen Trail update, we can even build our own outposts and customize them with different designs. We can now also experiment with weapon paints, which can be collected while exploring the maps.

Overall, this game is an absolute must-play for anyone who enjoys looting, hunting robots or fighting other players.

Frustrating Game ...
It looks amazing on the surface, but the more you play it, the more frustrating it gets.
The core of the game design is built in a way to reward you for playing like a jerk. Camping at an extraction point and shooting someone in the back is easier and more profitable than engaging in actual gameplay. No wonder this behavior is so widespread and so many players seem to accept it as part of the experience.

At the same time, PvE combat against the ARC machines is interesting and challenging. Yet, once again, the appearance of a player who seems to have no interest in fair play can ruin everything. As a result, you are forced to play stealthily and avoid almost everything and everyone as much as possible. But is this supposed to be a stealth game?

Progression is repetitive grinding in a nutshell. It feels surprisingly close to a Gacha game, except that you actually have to pay upfront to play it...

Storytelling? It's somewhere in there, but this game isn't really about the story. As a result, the narrative wasn't able to keep me playing for a long.

As verdict I can tell that despite its excellent visuals, atmospheric sound design, and genuinely fun PvE encounters, the overall experience becomes exhausting. A challenge is a good thing, but with this level of hostility and grinding, I eventually couldn't find an answer to a simple question: "Why should I pay for it and keep playing?"

Still, I'd like to express my sincere gratitude to the developers for offering the free weekend. I enjoyed certain aspects of the game and genuinely hated others, particularly situations over which I had no control. Unfortunately, there weren't enough positive moments to convince me to buy it and play it as a single player.
I also wouldn't recommend this game to anyone who doesn't want gaming to feel like a second job.

Easily one of the most boring games I've ever played. I don't understand what people see in it. Engaging robots isn't really worth it, just a waste of ammo, they're just too fat (bullet sponges). Engaging humans isn't worth it, because you get full inventory and overencumbered WAY before you get to a lift. I don't even understand why PvE players complain about the PvP part. Who the hell even shoots you? I never got shot at by players, because there's simply no reason to engage anyone or anything.

It's "cosmetic" multiplayer. The whole game is just a giant walking simulator, open world garbage collecting game, except it's bad even at that. I can't believe I actually prefer Ubisoft open world tower climbing games over this. You want a fun 3rd person PvE open world multiplayer game? Get Helldivers 2 or Space Marine 2. You want a fun PvP open world game? Apex Legends. What does this game - this entire genre even -  do, that some other game doesn't do better? There's no reason to play this.

The game has amzing audio design I guess? Very nice 3D audio simulation.
